text:
Columbus is 7-8-0, and the goalie has been the best thing about it. Cam Talbot has a .940 save rate and 8.6 goals saved above expected over his last five starts, 4-1-0, which explains a lot about how a team taking 45.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) has stayed close to .500.

Friday showed the other side. Buffalo led 5-1 after 40 minutes with a 33-18 shot edge, per NHL.com's Heather Engel, and Zach Werenski's power-play goal was all the Blue Jackets got back in a 5-2 loss.

The scoring is the real problem: 2.53 goals a game, 5.09 below what the chances deserved. Matthew Knies, on the top line with Adam Fantilli and Kent Johnson, has three points in his last 10 on 7.3 expected. That should turn. The Charlie Coyle, Mathieu Olivier and Cole Sillinger line has been the most productive, 7-5 in goals.

Only two of the seven wins have come in regulation, which matters in tiebreakers later. At a 16% playoff chance, Columbus needs Knies to heat up before Talbot cools off.
headline: Talbot is holding the line
